question: A team building a code-review assistant is deciding how granular to make the detected_pattern field on each structured finding. One option records only a broad category like "security" for every finding; another records the specific triggering construct, such as the exact function name, decorator, or regex rule that fired. Which choice better supports long-term analysis of developer dismissal patterns?
options: A) Neither option matters much, since dismissal rates should be analyzed through the severity field instead
B) The specific-construct option, since it lets the team isolate which exact rule causes a high dismissal rate and tune it
C) The broad-category option, since fewer distinct values are easier for a dashboard to render without extra grouping logic
D) The broad-category option, since recording specific constructs would expose proprietary rule names to the team
correct_answers: B) The specific-construct option, since it lets the team isolate which exact rule causes a high dismissal rate and tune it
explanations: Incorrect. Severity indicates how serious a finding is, not which specific construct or rule triggered it, so it cannot substitute for a pattern field when the goal is root-cause dismissal analysis.

Correct. A specific, construct-level detected_pattern value lets analysts pinpoint exactly which rule or code pattern is over-triggering, so the team can tune that particular rule instead of guessing across an entire broad category.
Incorrect. Rendering convenience does not outweigh the analytical value of granularity; a broad category collapses many distinct root causes into one bucket, making targeted tuning impossible.
Incorrect. The review team is the intended consumer of this data for tuning their own rules, so there is no confidentiality barrier that would justify withholding construct-level detail from them.
